statements.text: Trump Administration Imposes New Tariffs on Imported Trucks The administration announced 25% tariffs on imported medium- and heavy-duty trucks and parts, plus 10% on buses, starting Nov. 1 — aiming to boost U.S. manufacturing.
Companies with strong U.S. manufacturing footprints (e.g., Freightliner, Peterbilt, Kenworth, Mack) could benefit from reduced import competition.
Therefore, our Great Large Truck Company Manufacturers, such as Peterbilt, Kenworth, Freightliner, Mack Trucks, and others, will be protected from the onslaught of outside interruptions.

Some estimates suggest that a 25% import tariff combined with a 12% federal excise tax (FET) could raise the cost of a Class 8 tractor significantly — from around $170,000 to as much as $200,000+ or even $224,000 in some scenarios.
A 25% truck tariff aims to shield U.S. truck manufacturing, even though most trucks are assembled domestically.
Most heavy truck imports come from Mexico and Canada, and experts expect the new tariff to override USMCA provisions.
The kind of impact it will have will hinge on whether the tariff applies to truck parts and if it supersedes the U.S.-Mexico-Canada Agreement.
